meta.title: Harvard JCHS — State of the Nation's Housing
meta.source: Joint Center for Housing Studies of Harvard University
meta.report_name: The State of the Nation's Housing
meta.companion_report: The State of the Renter's Housing (also annual)
meta.methodology: JCHS publishes an annual flagship report drawing from ACS, AHS, HMDA, BLS QCEW, NAR, and Census BPS. Provides the national benchmark every state-level housing analysis is measured against. Key tables: cost burden by tenure × income tier, supply gap by metro, rent growth, household formation rate, homeownership rate by age, and homelessness counts. Cited in nearly every federal housing policy brief.

national_benchmarks.narrative: In 2024, 22.7 million US renter households (49 percent) were cost burdened, including 12.1 million (26 percent) with severe burdens; the number has risen by 2.3 million since 2019. JCHS puts the national housing shortfall at between 1.2 and 5.5 million units, citing other organizations' estimates. A record 771,480 people experienced homelessness on a single night in January 2024.
national_benchmarks.supply_gap_unavailable_reason: JCHS 2026 publishes no shortage estimate of its own; it reports other organizations' estimates of 1.2 to 5.5 million units.

colorado_context.narrative: JCHS 2026 names Colorado three times: active for-sale inventory in early 2026 was 32 percent above its 2019 level, one of 10 states above pre-pandemic levels; Colorado started a construction loan program for lower-cost homes in 2025; and Colorado is among the states permitting single-stairwell midrise buildings. For Colorado cost burden by county and place, use COHO's own ACS data rather than a national report.
